concepts.title: The Human Eye - Structure and Working

questions.q: How does the eye change focus for near and far objects?
questions.a: Ciliary muscles alter the lens thickness (curvature), changing its focal length - accommodation.

questions.q: What happens to the pupil in bright light?
questions.a: The iris makes the pupil smaller, limiting the light entering the eye.

questions.q: Why is a normal eye's near point 25 cm?
questions.a: Below this the lens cannot thicken further, so close objects blur - 25 cm is the least comfortable distance.

concepts.title: Defects of Vision and Their Correction

questions.q: What lens corrects myopia and why?
questions.a: A concave (diverging) lens, because it spreads rays so the image forms back on the retina of an elongated eyeball.

questions.q: What lens corrects hypermetropia and why?
questions.a: A convex (converging) lens, which adds convergence so near objects focus on the retina.

concepts.title: Dispersion, Scattering and the Colourful Sky

questions.q: Why does a prism split white light?
questions.a: Different colours refract by different amounts since their speeds in glass differ; violet bends most, red least.

questions.q: Why is the sun reddish at sunrise and sunset?
questions.a: Light crosses thicker air; blue is scattered away, letting mostly red reach the eye.

questions.q: What causes the twinkling of stars?
questions.a: Atmospheric refraction through moving air layers changes the star's apparent brightness and position.
